question.prompt: Run caller.php. legacy.php has no strict_types declaration. Which text does the caller print?
options: An empty string
TypeError
question.explanation: The strict caller passes a string to an int parameter. The call raises TypeError before the function body executes; the catch prints TypeError. The included file’s coercive mode does not control this call.

code.title: Two files in the same directory

files.name: caller.php
files.snippet:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
require __DIR__ . '/legacy.php';
try {
    echo formatTotal('12');
} catch (TypeError $error) {
    echo 'TypeError';
}

files.name: legacy.php
files.snippet:
<?php
function formatTotal(int $amount): string {
    return number_format($amount, 2, '.', '');
}

options: too large
unsupported
png

question.explanation: 2 * 1024 * 1024 equals 2097152. The test uses >, so an exactly two-MiB upload is accepted. The PNG MIME arm returns the extension png.

files.name: main.php
files.snippet:
<?php
function chooseExtension(string $detectedMime, int $bytes): string {
    if ($bytes > 2 * 1024 * 1024) {
        throw new LengthException('too large');
    }
    return match ($detectedMime) {
        'image/png' => 'png',
        'image/jpeg' => 'jpg',
        default => throw new InvalidArgumentException('unsupported'),
    };
}
try {
    echo chooseExtension('image/png', 2097152);
} catch (LengthException | InvalidArgumentException $error) {
    echo $error->getMessage();
}

question.explanation: The cloned message receives its own changed headers array, so the original has no X-Trace header. Both messages reference the same body object, which now contains old!. Real PSR-7 streams may similarly be mutable; message immutability is not a deep-copy guarantee.

files.name: main.php
files.snippet:
<?php
final class Message {
    public function __construct(public array $headers, public object $body) {}
    public function withHeader(string $name, string $value): self {
